thread.title: Netflix downgraded at KeyBanc due to pace of spending and length of time for a return

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: Netflix downgraded at KeyBanc due to pace of spending and length of time for a return
text:
Netflix is spending at an elevated clip and the returns on its investments may not materialize soon.
That is the view of KeyBanc analysts, who downgraded the streaming-video provider to sector weight from overweight on the heels of blowout results that sent shares NFLX, +4.38% soaring late Tuesday. The stock was up 7% in early trade Wednesday.
Netflix has no problem in growing its subscriber base, but “substantial upside” for shares from here will require further revenue growth and accelerating profits, which have not grown as fast as the entertainment giant hoped, said Andy Hargreaves and a team at KeyBanc, in a note to clients.
See Also The Man Behind the World's Biggest Private-Equity Insolvency × “While we maintain a favorable view of Netflix’s strategic positioning, we believe improving investment efficiency or significant ancillary opportunities are needed to drive upside from current levels, and we don’t anticipate either over the next year,” said a team of KeyBanc analysts led by Andy Hargreaves.
Netflix added a net 6.96 million subscribers in the third quarter, blowing past expectations , after a second-quarter miss on those numbers, which sent shares careening lower in July . The Los Gatos, Calif., company sees more subscribers hopping on board in the fourth quarter. But it also plans on maintaining its spending rate, estimates KeyBanc’s analysts, who forecast free cash flow of around negative $3 billion for 2018 — in line with Netflix’s own estimates.
Read: Netflix is ditching freeloaders from subscriber forecasts after volatile stock moves
“We believe Netflix’s leadership position in subscription video provides long-term opportunities to build revenue in consumer products, advertising, broad theatrical releases, and mobile-only subscriptions,” said Hargreaves and the team. But those opportunities could take “several years to develop” and are at risk from rising interest rates and growing competition over the next year.
Netflix shares have shot up 80% this year so far, making it the fourth-best performing stock among constituents of the S&P 500 SPX, -0.05% The company, run by Reed Hastings, also has outperformed a clutch of highflying technology and internet-related stocks known as FAANG—Facebook Inc. FB, +0.09% Apple Inc. AAPL, -0.51% Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, +0.30% and Alphabet’s Google Inc. GOOGL, -0.70%
Raymond James and Goldman Sachs recently cut their price targets , citing investor jitters over rising interest rates and trade tensions. However, they were upbeat on Netflix’s long-term prospects, while Citigroup lifted Netflix to buy from neutral last Friday, saying last week’s two-day market rout was a chance to pick up the stock.
Even after the June results that sent shares tumbling, Wall Street analysts largely stood by the company , including KeyBanc, though they lowered their share price target to $375.
“Given our positive ongoing view of the business, a lower stock price or evidence of improving investment efficiency would likely prompt us to resume a more-positive view of the shares,” said the analysts.
Analysts at Wedbush, who have been bearish on Netflix for some time due to the company’s continued cash burn and negative free cash flow, nudged the firm's 12-month price target up to $150 from $125. Maintaining their underperform rating, they said they “see clouds on the horizon.”
“Disney DIS, +0.75% and Fox FOXA, -0.07% are likely to migrate content that is currently licensed to Netflix to a Disney-sponsored standalone service next year,” they wrote. “This subjects the company to the potential for slowing subscriber growth should its original content offering fail to achieve the quality and quantity of the lost content.”
But others continued their bullish streak Wednesday, with analysts at Morgan Stanley raising their price target to $475 from $450 while maintaining their overweight rating. Netflix “has consistently reinvested its near-term success into deepening its competitive moat,” which has “allowed it to find success,” they wrote.
J.P. Morgan raised its price target to $450 from $415 while maintaining an overweight rating. “We believe 3Q results and the 4Q guide indicate that Netflix is back on track. While quarters can be lumpy, the bigger path is consistent and we continue to believe there is significant growth potential ahead,” analysts wrote. Netflix is forecasting fourth-quarter net additions of 9.4 million and paid net additions of 7.6 million.
Analysts seemed convinced by Netflix's reassurances about its negative free cash burn. The streaming giant is “approaching where the growth in operating profit is going to grow faster than our growth in content cash spend,” Netflix Chief Financial Officer David Wells said during Tuesday’s earnings interview, adding that free cash flow burn in 2019 would be roughly flat compared to 2018.
“This shows that the worst of the investment phase is mostly over,” Raymond James analyst Justin Patterson told MarketWatch. “We should see Netflix turn free cash flow positive in the next few years.”
Stifel, Piper Jaffray, Raymond James and Cowen & Co., all pushed their price targets up well into the $400 range, rating the company at overweight or outperform equivalents based on strong third-quarter numbers and fourth-quarter forecasts.
